newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower but above new contract lows.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower but above new contract lows.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower, but a short-covering rally helped wheat close above Monday's new contract lows, traders said.
"We sold it deep enough that we got to the point where there was no further follow-through selling," a trader said.
KCBT wheat was undermined by news Egypt bought 450,0000 tonnes of French wheat over the weekend at values that were $10 to $15 cheaper than U.S. prices.
Wheat was also burdened by spillover pressure from CBOT soybeans, which were sharply lower on forecasts for overall good growing weather.
Weekend rains also doused the central Plains, brightening prospects for fall planting of HRW wheat. One grain dealer characterized planting conditions as "excellent."
KCBT wheat closed 4-3/4 to eight cents per bushel lower, with Sept down 5-1/4 cents at $4.33-1/4. Dec ended down 4-3/4 cents at $4.25-1/4, just above the new contract low of $4.21.
Traders said Dreyfus' Term Commodities bought 2.8 million Dec bushels and Refco bought 2.6 million Dec. CIS sold 1.3 million March. FIMAT bought 1.1 million Dec, they said.
The KCBT pegged Monday's wheat volume at 37.3 million bushels, versus Friday's volume of 31.31 million.
